subject: Hosted pilot access plan, throttle targets, and prefetch asks
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wong <alex.wong@finly.com>, Maya Desai <maya.desai@finly.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted pilot access plan, throttle targets, and prefetch asks

Hi Alex / Maya — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your Hosted pilot started without surprises. I pasted an action checklist below; please confirm the items we flagged as blockers (marked ACTION).

Summary from the call
- Goal: proof-of-concept for customer-support summarization + routing (approx. 500–800 tokens per request on average).
- Preference expressed: prefer Hosted API if compliance/latency OK; exploring Dedicated only if egress/residency or strict SLA required.

Proposed quickstart plan (high level) — ACTION: confirm numbers
1) Sandbox endpoints: we’ll provision a sandbox endpoint named finly-sandbox-1.
   - Default ratecap: 20 TPS (steady), burst to 50 TPS for short spikes (30s).
   - Concurrent requests: configure 30 concurrent streams.
2) Token budgeting: please confirm expected avg tokens per call (you mentioned ~600 tokens).
3) Traffic profile: please confirm expected steady RPS (you said ~10 TPS steady today) and expected peak windows (e.g., morning batch).
4) Security/compliance: ACTION: please confirm whether Finly needs Private VPC or on-prem for the pilot; if not, Hosted with KMS + audit logs should suffice.

Prefetch/prefix/cache suggestion
- For support summaries we recommend enabling prefix KV cache and short-term response caching for identical prompts (saves tokens and improves tail latency). If you expect many warm prefixes, we can pre-warm caches during the sandbox ramp.

Attachments included: redwood-quickstart-pack.pdf (quickstart checklist, endpoint names, sample curl), sandbox-credentials.txt (one-time token for sandbox).

Next steps
- ACTION (Finly): confirm avg tokens and expected steady + peak TPS.
- ACTION (Redwood): provision sandbox endpoint and share credentials once we have the confirmed traffic numbers.
- Tech sync: Ben (SE) to run a 45-min technical setup + perf tuning call next week. Jordan (AE) will send dates.

If you want an initial cost estimate for the pilot (per-token model + expected traffic), reply with the traffic numbers and we’ll send a short worksheet.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — this is helpful. Confirming items from our side:
- We want to try Hosted for the pilot (lower ops overhead) but we do need SLA visibility (99.9% target) and burst capacity for business hours spikes.
- Traffic: current expectation is ~10 TPS steady, with peaks up to 35 TPS during email digest batches (these peaks last ~2–5 minutes). Average payload is 550–700 tokens (your 600 estimate is correct).
- Security: we don’t need an on-prem solution for the pilot. We will request SOC2 evidence and a quick KMS/keys architecture note.

ACTION: I attached a simple capacity sheet (capacity_requirements.xlsx) with our assumptions; Ben, Jordan — happy to sync next week.

Also: Can you add a short note on throttling behavior (429 vs queueing) and how burst is handled for Hosted endpoints? That will help my infra team plan retries.

–Alex

On Sun, Aug 30, 2026 at 9:08 AM Alex Wong <alex.wong@finly.com> wrote:
> Thanks Kimberly — this is helpful. Confirming items from our side:
> - We want to try Hosted for the pilot ...

Thanks for the quick confirm, Alex — answered inline and proposed next steps:

Throttling behavior (short answer)
- Hosted endpoints enforce per-endpoint rate limits with soft-burst windows. Excess requests beyond the burst window receive 429s.
- We expose retry-recommendations: exponential backoff + jitter; for short spikes we typically recommend 3 retries with 200ms base.
- If you want automatic request queuing instead of immediate 429s, we can enable a small request queue for the sandbox endpoint (adds up to ~500ms tail latency). Let us know preference.

Prefetch/prefix plan — recommended
- Enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts (helps reduce tokens consumed).
- If you have predictable warm prefixes (e.g., standard support templates), Ben can instrument a pre-warm script during ramp.

Proposed schedule
- Technical sync (Ben): 45 mins — Ben will demo prefetch + caching and walk through endpoint settings.
- Commercial sync (Jordan): 15 mins to confirm SLA expectations and ramp timeline.

ACTION ITEMS
- Alex (Finly): confirm whether you prefer 429s or queueing for short spikes.
- Finly: confirm peak duration for the 35 TPS spikes (you said 2–5 minutes; we’ll use 5m for planning unless updated).
- Redwood: we’ll provision finly-sandbox-1 with 20 TPS steady + 50 TPS burst and enable the optional queue (off by default) if you request it.

I’ll send calendar invites once you confirm your preference for queueing vs immediate 429s.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
